units.section: INTRO
units.spoken: Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3)

units.section: INTRO
units.spoken: A robot-arm learner that scores its turning forces with two networks, takes the lower score, and updates the actor less often than the critics.

sections.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Section one, Why the scoring network rates moves too high

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) trains one network, the actor, to output a robot arm's turning forces and a second, the critic, to score them, and the scorer often rates some turning forces too high, so the actor follows those errors. On a real arm, a torque the actor picks because its score is too high is a wasted or harmful move.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The agent is the learner that picks the moves. A state is the agent's situation right now. A move, or action, is one choice the agent can make in a state. A reward is the number the world hands back after each move, good or bad. On a robot, sensing, moving and scoring repeat many times every second.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) is DDPG with three changes that reduce them. Each change tackles one way those errors grow.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The running example is the Reacher task from Unity ML-Agents, a toolkit for training agents inside game worlds, as specified in the project: a robot arm with two joints whose actions are four torques. A torque is a turning force a motor applies at a joint. On the Reacher each torque is a number from -1 to 1. Every step the arm senses its state, 33 numbers describing the position, rotation and speed of its parts, and earns 0.1 whenever its hand is inside a moving goal. So the hand must follow the goal as it moves, not just reach it once. The task counts as solved when the arm averages plus 30 over 100 episodes in a row.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Take a look at this figure. The arm has two joints, a shoulder and an elbow, each turning about two axes. Four torques, one per axis, turn the joints. The hand hangs just short of the goal ball. The lesson is the task: turn the joints so the hand lands on the moving goal, and keep following it as it moves.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The arm in Figure 1 stands near a dashed goal circle that moves. One step: the arm reads its 33 numbers, sends four torques, and earns 0.1 when its hand is inside the goal.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The return is all the reward still to come, with later rewards counted a little less. A move's value Q of s and a, also called its score, is the return the agent expects if it makes move a in state s and plays on from there. DDPG, which TD3 changes, learns two networks.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The deterministic actor mu sub thay-ta is a network with weights thay-ta that outputs one action every time, with no random draw. The critic Q sub fee is a network with weights fee that scores a state and an action together; its score stands for the return the agent expects. On the Reacher nothing stops the critic from scoring some of the arm's torques too high.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: 1.1 The actor follows scores that were never real

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Overestimation

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: What. Overestimation means the values rise above the return the arm really earns, because the critic's scores carry errors and the actor's search plays the role of the max, the highest score, following the gradient, the uphill direction, toward the highest score, including where the critic is wrong.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: How. The actor update follows the gradient up, so it moves toward the highest score.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Why. The actor follows scores that were never real, and the critic's estimate sits above the true value and stays there.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Take a look at this figure. Two lines run across time: the true value stays near its level, and the critic's estimate sits above it and stays there. The lesson is the problem: the critic's scores run too high, and the actor follows scores that were never real.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The critic's estimate sits above the true value over time while the true value stays near its level. Figure 2 is a sketch, not measured data.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: 1.2 Why Double DQN's fix does not carry over to DDPG

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The slow copy

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: What. The critic learns by being pulled toward a target, the number its scores move toward, and that target moves whenever the critic moves, so the critic follows its own changes. A target network is a slow copy of the network being trained, updated a little at a time, that computes the targets.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: How. The live network learns while the slow copy stands almost still, so the target holds still while the critic learns.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Why. The critic's scores move toward a target that barely moves between updates, instead of following their own changes.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: The target is the step's reward plus its own score for what comes next, counted a little less. The Deep Q-Network (DQN) scores its moves with one network, its Q-network. DQN had the same problem of a target that moves, and fixed it with a second network.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: In the value methods, which learn by scoring moves, the critic is the Q-network, the network that scores a state and a move together.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: In DDPG both the actor and the critic have a slow copy, marked by a prime on the weights, and the targets are built from those copies. The live networks are the actor and critic being trained, with weights thay-ta and fee.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: For value methods, overestimation already has a known fix. Double DQN is a fix for DQN that uses two networks inside the target, with only one live network, the Q-network. Double DQN's target lets the live network pick the next move and the target network score it. (Double DQN) Between Double DQN and the min, taking the lower of two scores, sits a pair version: two actors, two critics, two targets, each actor's torques scored by the other's critic. TD3 runs the single-actor version: one actor, both critics scoring its torques. TD3 borrows this check, so one high score gets caught.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: In DDPG the same trick would let the live actor pick the next torques and a slow critic score them. But the live actor chose those torques for their high live-critic scores. The slow critic scores them nearly the same, because the slow copies stay close to the live networks. Pick and score come from nearly the same network, so the score stays too high.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: 1.3 Errors grow through the target

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Bootstrapping: errors carry forward

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: What. Picture three value boxes in a chain, each feeding the next target: a small error in the first box is carried into the second and grows in the third. Bootstrapping means putting the critic's current guess for the next state inside the target.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: How. Each target is built from the critic's own next score, so an error at one step is carried into the next.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Why. One fix on its own is not enough: a lower score alone would still feed the next target, and a slower actor alone would still follow an inflated critic.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Take a look at this figure. Three boxes feed each next target in a chain. A small error in the first box is carried into the second and grows larger in the third. The lesson is the carry-forward: each target is built from the critic's own scores, so one error feeds the next.

units.section: 1 Why the scoring network rates moves too high
units.spoken: Three value boxes in Figure 3 feed each next target. The error bar under each box grows from box to box: small, carried forward, then grown larger.

sections.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Section two, Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Target policy smoothing

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: What. The slow actor names one set of next torques, and the critic may score that set too high, one high score, made noisy by the critic's errors, over one set of torques. A policy is the agent's rule for choosing a move in each state; here the policy is the actor.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: How. A small random nudge is added to the next torques inside the target only, clipped to stay inside its limit, so the critics score the torques around the pick as well as the pick itself.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Why. Torques close together score about the same, so no one torque scores far above its neighbours: no lone high score for the actor to follow.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Two critics, the lower score

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: What. Two slow critics score the same nudged torques side by side. The target takes the lower score, and the two live critics learn toward that target.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: How. Both live critics learn from the same batches and target, and the lower slow score sets the target.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Why. One high score made noisy by the critic's errors gets caught: a torque the critic scores too low is avoided by the actor, so that error is not followed and carried forward.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Delayed actor updates

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: What. The actor learns from a critic that is still changing, so each update follows a moving target. TD3 moves the actor and the slow copies only once every d critic updates, where d, the delay, is 2.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: How. The critics update every step while the actor waits, so the actor follows a critic with steadied scores.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Why. The actor's torques shift toward scores that stay steady across both critics, instead of following each new shift.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Take a look at this figure. Five boxes run from random past steps through target, critic and actor to the slow copies. Three of the boxes carry the TD3 changes: the target is smoothed, the critics are doubled with the lower score kept, and the actor updates less often. The lesson is the three changes in one picture: each one tackles one way the errors grow.

units.section: 2 Twin critics, a smoothed target and delayed actor updates
units.spoken: Five boxes in Figure 4 run from random past steps through target, critic and actor to the slow copies, with the three TD3 changes highlighted.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Section three, TD3's update, rule by rule

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: 3.1 Smoothing the next torques

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The DDPG critic's target is the step's reward plus the discounted score the slow critic gives to the slow actor's next torques. TD3 changes this target twice: it nudges the next torques and takes the lower score. Replay keeps a memory of past steps, and training draws random batches. The discount gamma sets how much a reward one step later still counts.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Equation 1. Smoothing the next torques. The target scores not one set of torques but the torques around it: a small clipped nudge joins the slow actor's pick, so nearby torques score about the same.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. The target scores not one set of torques but the torques around it: a small clipped nudge joins the slow actor's pick, so nearby torques score about the same.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The first line. N is the nudge, one small random shift per torque. Clip holds its result between minus c and c, the clip limit. Tilde sigma is the nudge's size. Xi is a fresh random draw, one per torque. A standard bell is centred at zero with width one. Tilde sigma times xi is a draw scaled to that size. N equals a draw scaled to the nudge's size, clipped between minus c and c. Intuitively, each torque gets its own small random shift, so the target scores the torques around the pick.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. One exact set of torques can score far above its neighbours, so the target scores the neighbouring torques too.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. The slow actor's next torques: the nudge shifts each one a little, so the target scores a little neighbourhood, not one point.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The second line. A tilde is the smoothed next torques. Those are the torques the target will score. Mu sub thay-ta prime of s prime is the slow actor's next torques. S prime is the next state, the arm's 33 numbers after the step. The prime marks the slow copy. Plus n adds the nudge. The nudge is a draw scaled to the nudge's size and clipped, one per torque. A tilde equals the slow actor's next torques plus the nudge. Intuitively, adding the nudge means similar torques score about the same, so no lone high score sets the target on its own.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The target must score the torques the arm will actually meet, smoothed, not the raw pick.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. One next state: the slow actor names its torques, the nudge shifts them, and those smoothed torques go to the critics.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The third line. A tilde on the left is the smoothed torques. The arrow means is replaced by. The smoothed torques are replaced by the clipped version. Clip keeps each torque inside minus 1 and 1. A torque above 1 becomes 1. A torque below minus 1 becomes minus 1. One inside stays as it is. A tilde is replaced by its clipped version, each torque inside minus 1 and 1. Intuitively, the target never scores a torque the arm cannot give.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. A smoothed torque past the motor's limit is still a torque the arm cannot give.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. A smoothed torque the nudge pushed past 1: clip pins it at 1 before the critics score it.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: So the target scores the neighbouring torques, not one set, and the smoothed torques go to the critics.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: An arm whose hand is hovering just outside the moving goal, so the slow actor's next torques turn the elbow a little harder. The nudge shifts each torque a little in a random direction and the clip keeps them in range, so the target scores the neighbouring torques as well as the pick itself, and one lone high score in one critic cannot set the target on its own.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: 3.2 The lower of two critics

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The smoothed torques go to both slow critics.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Equation 2. The lower of two slow critics. Two slow critics score the same smoothed torques, and the target takes the lower score, so one high score cannot lift the target on its own.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. Two slow critics score the same smoothed torques, and the target takes the lower score, so one high score cannot lift the target on its own.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The first line. Y is the target, the number the live critics' scores are pulled toward. R is the reward stored with this step. Gamma is the discount, how much a reward one step later still counts. Min of i equals 1 to 2 takes the lower of the two scores. One score comes from each slow critic. Q sub fee prime 1 is slow critic 1's score. Q sub fee prime 2 is slow critic 2's score. Each scores the next state s prime with the smoothed torques a tilde. The target is the stored reward plus the discounted lower score for the nudged next torques. Intuitively, the min also favours steady scores: when a score swings widely, the lower of two draws lands further down, so states whose scores vary little keep the higher value, and the target stays steady.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. One critic on its own can lift the target with a noisy high score, so the target takes the lower score.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. The two slow critics score the same nudged torques, and the lower score sets the target, so one high score cannot lift it alone.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: So the target is the stored reward plus the discounted lower score, and both live critics learn toward it.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: A step where the hand is near the goal, so one slow critic scores the nudged torques high, while the other, which has seen those torques miss before, scores them lower. The target takes the lower score, so the live critics are pulled toward the lower number, not the higher one.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The TD3 paper swaps the letters: fee for the actor, thay-ta for the critics. Its pee sub fee is the actor's policy, the rule that picks the torques, and its epsilon is the target nudge. This page keeps thay-ta for the actor and fee for the critics.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: 3.3 Training both critics

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Each live critic then shrinks its own gap to that shared target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Equation 3. Training both critics. Each live critic learns from one shared target: the average squared gap between its score and that target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. Each live critic learns from one shared target: the average squared gap between its score and that target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The first line. L of fee sub i is the loss for live critic i. I is 1 or 2, so there is one loss per critic. The loss is a function of fee sub i, the live critic's weights. Changing the weights changes the scores and so changes the loss. L of fee sub i equals the average squared gap to the shared target. Intuitively, each critic gets its own loss, and both measure the gap to the same shared target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. Each live critic needs its own loss, since each has its own weights to move.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. Critic 1's weights: changing them changes its scores, so it changes critic 1's loss, not critic 2's.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The second line. E is the expected value, the batch average. Add the squared gaps over the batch and divide by its steps. Y is the shared target, the number both live critics learn toward. Q of fee sub i of s and a is live critic i's score. It scores the stored state s and torques a. The minus leaves the gap between target and score. The square makes the gap always positive, so big misses count more. So this half is each live critic's loss, the average squared gap to the shared target. Intuitively, sharing y trains both critics toward the same number, so the actor follows the same score from both critics.
termList: Q of fee sub i of s and a

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The two critics must learn toward the same number, or their scores differ.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. One stored step: both critics compare their own scores with the same target and shrink the gap.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: So each critic's loss is the average squared gap to the shared target, and both critics learn toward the same number.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: A batch where most stored steps score close to their target, while a few steps where the hand swung wide miss by a lot. Squaring makes those few wide misses count for more than the many small ones, so the loss pulls the critics hardest where they are most wrong, and both critics move toward the same target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: 3.4 The delayed actor and slow copies

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Until that update comes, the actor keeps its old weights.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Equation 4. The delayed actor and slow copies. The actor and the slow copies move only every second critic update, once the critics' scores have steadied enough to follow.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. The actor and the slow copies move only every second critic update, once the critics' scores have steadied enough to follow.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The first line. G sub 1 is critic 1's uphill direction for the torques. It is the way to shift them so its score rises. Nabla sub a is the gradient with respect to the torques. It is how the score changes as the torques change. Q of fee sub 1 of s and a is critic 1's score. It scores the state s and the torques a the actor picks. G sub 1 equals the gradient of critic 1's score, the way each torque should shift to raise the score. Intuitively, both critics learn toward the same target, so one gradient is enough, and the paper guides the actor with the first critic.
termList: Q of fee sub 1 of s and a

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The actor needs a direction, not a number: which way to shift each torque so the score rises.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. The elbow torque: critic 1's slope says which way to shift it to raise the score.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The second line. J is the actor's expected return. Nabla sub thay-ta of J is how J changes when the weights thay-ta move. E is the batch average. Add the per-state products over the batch and divide by its steps. G sub 1 is the direction the torques should shift to raise critic 1's score. Nabla sub thay-ta of mu sub thay-ta of s is the actor's slope. It is how the actor's torques move when its weights move. So the product is how the return changes through the torques. The approx sign means the batch average stands in for the true average. So the return's slope is about that average. Intuitively, this is the DDPG actor update using critic 1 only, with the lower score needed only in the target.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The actor's weights move through the torques, so the slope chains through the actor to the weights.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. One state in the batch: the slope through the torques times the slope through the actor gives the slope for the weights.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The third line. Fee prime sub i are the slow critics' weights, with i 1 or 2. The prime marks a slow copy. Fee sub i are the live critics' weights, and tau is the small share. Tau times fee sub i takes a small share of the live weights. One minus tau times fee prime sub i keeps the rest of the slow weights. The two shares add to one. So each slow weight takes only a small step toward its live weight. The arrow means is replaced by. Each slow weight is replaced by this blend. Here it runs every d-th update, not after every update. Intuitively, the slow critics follow the live critics a little at a time, so the target holds almost still while the critics learn.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The slow critics must change by only a small share, or the target follows the live networks.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. One slow critic weight: it takes only a small step toward its live weight, so the target barely moves.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: The fourth line. Thay-ta prime are the slow actor's weights, the prime marking the slow copy. Thay-ta are the live actor's weights. Tau times thay-ta takes a small share of the live weights. One minus tau times thay-ta prime keeps the rest of the slow weights. The two shares add to one. So each slow weight takes only a small step toward its live weight. The arrow means is replaced by. Each slow weight is replaced by this blend. Here it runs every d-th update, not after every update. The actor's weights move along the direction critic 1 gives. Intuitively, the slow actor follows the live actor a little at a time, so the targets stay steady while the actor learns.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Intuition. The slow actor changes by only a small share, so the next torques it names stay close to the old ones.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: Example. One slow actor weight: it takes only a small step toward its live weight, so its next torques barely change.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: So every second critic update the actor moves along critic 1's uphill direction, and the slow copies each take a small share of their live weights.

units.section: 3 TD3's update, rule by rule
units.spoken: A batch where critic 1's slope for the elbow torque is clear, while the slow actor's torques still follow the old direction. The actor's weights move a step along the slope, and the slow copies take only a small share of the move, so the target the critics follow next stays almost where it was.

units.spoken: The third line. The arrow means is replaced by. A tilde is replaced by its clipped version, each torque held inside minus 1 and 1, so the target never scores a torque the arm cannot give.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 4 the smoothed torques are held inside what the arm can give.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. A smoothed torque past 1 is pinned at 1 before the critics score it.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The fourth line. Y is the target the live critics learn toward. R is the stored reward. The plus adds the discounted lower slow score. Y equals the stored reward plus the discounted lower slow score.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 5 the target is built from the reward and the future.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. One stored step brings its reward, the first part of the target.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The fifth line. Gamma is the discount: the future counts a little less. Q sub fee prime sub i is a slow critic's score, and min of i equals 1 to 2 takes the lower of the two slow critics' scores, so one high score cannot lift the target on its own.
termList: Q sub fee prime sub i

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 5 the lower slow score sets the future part.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. Both slow critics score the same torques; the lower score goes into the target.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The sixth line. L of fee sub i is the loss for live critic i, with i 1 or 2. The loss counts as the average squared gap to the shared target.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 6 each live critic gets its own loss.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. Critic 1's loss is a function of critic 1's weights, so moving them moves only its loss.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The seventh line. E is the batch average over the batch's squared gaps. Each gap is the target minus live critic i's score Q of fee sub i of s and a, squared so big misses count more.
termList: Q of fee sub i of s and a

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 6 the loss is the average squared gap over the batch.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. One stored step's gap is squared, and each critic shrinks the average.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The eighth line. G sub 1 is critic 1's uphill direction for the torques, the gradient of critic 1's score: the way to shift each torque so its score rises. This direction is chained through the actor, where the batch average of the uphill direction times the actor's slope moves the actor's weights.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 7, on every d-th update only, critic 1 gives the direction the torques should shift.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. The elbow torque's slope says which way to shift it to raise critic 1's score.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The ninth line. J is the actor's expected return, and nabla sub thay-ta of J is how J changes when the weights move. The approx sign means the batch average stands in for the true average. This is the DDPG actor update using critic 1 only, and it runs only every d-th update.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 8 the actor's weights move along the slope chained through the torques.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. One state in the batch gives its slope through the torques times its slope through the actor.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The tenth line. Fee prime sub i are the slow critics' weights, with i 1 or 2, the prime marking a slow copy. Each slow weight takes a small share tau of its live weight and keeps the rest, so it takes only a small step toward the live network.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 9 both slow critics blend a small step toward the live critics.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. One slow critic weight takes only a small step toward its live weight.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: The eleventh line. Thay-ta prime are the slow actor's weights. Each slow weight takes a small share tau of its live weight and keeps the rest, every d-th update.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Intuition. At stage 10 the slow actor blends a small step toward the live actor, closing the update.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: Example. One slow actor weight takes only a small step toward its live weight, so its next torques barely change.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: So one TD3 update runs from a random batch to the slow copies blending, with the actor moving and the slow copies blending every second update.

units.section: 4 One TD3 update on a Reacher batch
units.spoken: One batch drawn from replay: the hand missed the goal on most stored steps, so the targets stay low, while on the few steps inside the goal the lower slow score keeps the target near the true value, and the actor moves only on every second update.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Section five, TD3's update in PyTorch

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: An episode is one run from start to end. Each episode is also cut off after a fixed number of steps; that cut is not a real end, so the target keeps its next-state term.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This code runs one TD3 update. It smooths the next torques with a clipped nudge, builds the target from the reward and the lower slow score, moves both critics toward that shared target, and every second update moves the actor and blends the slow copies. The lesson is the whole update in one function: smooth, target, critics, then actor and slow copies on every second update.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: 1. First, the smoothing of the next torques: target_noise is the nudge's size and c is the clip limit. s2 is the next state. The outer clamp keeps each torque in range.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: 2. Next, the target from the lower slow score: under torch.no_grad() the target is computed without tracking gradients, so no update runs on it. gamma in the code is the discount gamma, how much a reward one step later still counts. done is 1 on a real end and 0 on a time-limit cut, so the future value is kept when the episode was cut short and dropped on a real end.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: 3. Then, the critics' loss: both live critics move toward the one target. F.mse_loss is the mean squared gap. The critics' optimizer clears the critics' gradients before the backward pass, the pass that carries each error back through the network to move the weights, so gradients do not carry over across updates.

units.section: 5 TD3's update in PyTorch
units.spoken: 4. Last, the actor and the slow copies: every d-th update only, the actor loss is minus the critic's score of the actor's torques, so lowering the loss raises the score. step counts the updates, so the actor block runs only on every d-th update. critic_opt and actor_opt are the optimizers that apply the critics' and the actor's updates. The actor's optimizer clears the actor's gradients before its backward pass. actor_t, q1_t and q2_t are the slow copies: the _t names the target copy. lerp_ moves each slow weight toward its live weight by the small share tau, tau, changing the weight itself rather than making a copy, one pair at a time: one slow weight and its live weight.

units.section: 6 One critic against twin critics
units.spoken: Section six, One critic against twin critics

units.section: 6 One critic against twin critics
units.spoken: The tool reuses the critic's own guess round after round, which is bootstrapping. A round is one pass over a single torque line, where the actor jumps to the highest point it sees.

units.section: 6 One critic against twin critics
units.spoken: Take a look at this figure. The same rounds run twice, once with one critic and once with the lower of two scores. With one critic, the target bar stands above the true value; with the lower score, the bar sits near it. Raising the error or the rounds lifts the one-critic bar higher, and with no error both sit near the true value. The lesson is the comparison: the lower score keeps the target near the true value.

units.section: 6 One critic against twin critics
units.spoken: The same rounds in Figure 6 run twice, once with one critic and once with the lower score, so the two targets can be compared. The one-critic bar stands above the dashed true-value line while the lower-of-two bar sits near it; raising the error or the rounds lifts the one-critic bar higher, and with no error both sit near the true value.

units.section: 6 One critic against twin critics
units.spoken: Try the tool. Set the critic error and the rounds of reusing its own guess, then press New run. Watch the one-critic target stand above the true value while the lower-of-two target sits near it. Raising the error or the rounds lifts the one-critic bar higher, and with no error both sit near the true value.

sections.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Section seven, How TD3 is trained and how it compares

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 7.1 One critic update per step, actor updates less often

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Every step the arm takes stores one step and runs one critic update; the actor and the slow copies update every d critic updates. Exploration noise is a small random nudge added to the actor's actions while it learns, so the agent tries moves it is not sure about. While the arm acts, TD3 draws this noise fresh each step.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Each step costs one critic update covering both critics on a batch of 100, about twice the critic work of one DDPG step; every second step adds one actor update and the slow-copy blends. Memory holds two live critics, one actor, three slow copies, plus the replay buffer: one more live critic and slow copy than DDPG.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Evaluation means testing the trained actor with exploration switched off, so the tests are noise-free.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Before learning starts, the first stretch of steps uses random actions, a warm-up. Noise drawn fresh each step worked as well as the drifting noise DDPG uses, which carries each step's nudge into the next, so its nudges change slowly. The drifting noise offered no performance benefits, so TD3 keeps the simpler noise.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Stable-Baselines3, a widely used reinforcement learning code library, runs this update, with two critics and a delayed actor.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: The seven tasks in the comparison are a running half cheetah, a one-legged hopper, a two-legged walker, a four-legged ant, a reaching arm (Reacher), a pendulum, and a double pendulum.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 7.2 The three settings that shape TD3

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Three settings shape TD3 itself; the rest are the usual network sizes and training setup. Each one below says what raising it and lowering it does.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 1. Target nudge size tilde sigma 0.2, clip limit c 0.5. A bigger nudge smooths the critic over a wider neighbourhood but blurs the true scores; a smaller nudge keeps the target sharp but lets one lone high score survive.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 2. Delay d 2. The actor and the slow copies move only every second critic update. A longer delay lets the actor learn from a critic whose scores have steadied more, but the actor learns more slowly.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 3. Soft-update share tau 0.005. Each slow weight takes this share of its live weight at each blend. A bigger share tracks the live networks faster but moves the target more; a smaller share holds the target still but lags further behind.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: 7.3 TD3 against other methods on simulated robot tasks

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: A seed is a starting number that fixes the random draws: one seed, one full training run. Each method ran 1 million steps per task, 10 runs from 10 seeds. Every 5,000 steps, the actor's average return over 10 episodes with no exploration noise was recorded.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), another way to train an actor that makes small, careful updates and learns only from fresh steps, is one of the methods compared. Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) is compared too: it draws its torques from a range, a spread of likely torques in each state, instead of committing to one set, so it explores more widely. The full comparison set is TD3, DDPG, the authors' retuned DDPG, PPO, TRPO, which caps each update, ACKTR, an actor-critic with fast approximate updates, and SAC.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: The comparison runs on those seven tasks in MuJoCo, a physics simulator used for robot tasks, through Gym, a standard collection of reinforcement learning tasks. The Reacher in the comparison is a smaller simulated arm from Gym, not the Unity ML-Agents Reacher of the running example: it senses 11 numbers and takes 2 torques.

units.section: 7 How TD3 is trained and how it compares
units.spoken: The paper's measured estimates put the lower-of-two target near the true value and the one-critic target above it. TD3 scored best on five of the seven tasks, tied at 1000 on the pendulum, and scored below DDPG on the double pendulum. On the pendulum 1000 is the top score: 1 per step for staying upright over 1000 steps, a perfect run. One change alone lifts scores little in most cases. The lower-score rule alone lifts Ant from 564 to 3819. Pairs lift scores much higher. The full version is best on Hopper and Ant of the four tasks. DQ-AC, the pair version with two actors and two critics, and DDQN-AC, the single-actor version that lets the live actor pick and the slow critic score, were compared against the clipped double-Q version, the lower-of-two-scores rule, with the same delay and smoothing.

units.section: 8 When TD3 fits
units.spoken: Section eight, When TD3 fits

units.section: 8 When TD3 fits
units.spoken: TD3 fits when the moves are continuous, old steps are worth reusing, and a deterministic actor is wanted. A deterministic actor is cheap to run once trained, since it outputs its torques directly. It also fits when DDPG's critic scores too high or training is unstable: it keeps DDPG's replay memory and actor, adds a second live critic and a second slow critic, and makes the three changes.

units.section: 8 When TD3 fits
units.spoken: When exploration is hard, or the settings must work across tasks without tuning, Soft Actor-Critic, the next page, is worth trying.

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: Section nine, How TD3 fails

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: 1. Target nudge too large. The critic blurs over too wide a neighbourhood and learning slows, so shrink the nudge's size or its clip. From the mechanism, not a paper measurement.

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: 2. Delay too large. The actor waits too long between updates and learns too slowly, so update the actor more often. From the mechanism, not a paper measurement.

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: 3. Still poor exploration on hard tasks. A deterministic actor plus fixed noise cannot reach new moves, so try Soft Actor-Critic, the next page. From the mechanism, not a paper measurement.

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: 4. The lower score too pessimistic on simple tasks. Underestimated torques are simply avoided by the actor, so it is usually harmless, and the fix is to keep the lower score. The TD3 paper states that underestimated actions are avoided by the policy.

units.section: 9 How TD3 fails
units.spoken: 5. Skipping the random-action warm-up. Early training leans on the actor's starting weights, so keep the warm-up. The TD3 paper starts with random actions to remove that dependence.
